faq.body: The product is intentionally focused for stage 1: read-only monitoring, decision support, and faster reviews for concentrated liquidity operators.

1.answer: No. Stage 1 is read-only by design. You connect wallets to monitor positions, understand performance, and receive action signals without giving the product execution power.
1.question: Does {{siteName}} move funds or rebalance positions?

2.answer: Explorers and generic dashboards show fragments. {{siteName}} is built to answer the actual operator questions: what needs attention, what is really making money, and whether action is worth the gas.
2.question: Why not just use an explorer or a generic analytics dashboard?

3.answer: Anyone can sign up, but the strongest fit is active LPs with concentrated liquidity positions who want better monitoring, cleaner performance visibility, and less manual checking.
3.question: Who gets the most value from the first version?

4.answer: Because trust matters. You should be able to understand your positions and workflows first. Execution and automation can come later, once monitoring, signals, and operator trust are solid.
4.question: Why start read-only?

faq.title: The first version is focused on one job: making LP management less noisy.

problem.body: Being an LP is supposed to feel like capital at work. In practice it often feels like babysitting: missed range moves, unclear profitability, too many tabs, and constant second-guessing about whether action is even worth the gas.

1.body: Positions drift toward the edge, go out of range, and quietly stop doing useful work unless you keep checking them.
1.title: Missed range moves

2.body: Fees look good in isolation, but it is hard to tell whether you are actually ahead after gas, inactive time, and position management.
2.title: Fake profitability

3.body: Wallets, explorers, dashboards, pool views, and spreadsheets all show fragments. None of them feel like one operating surface.
3.title: Fragmented tracking

4.body: Even when a position looks unhealthy, the real question is whether touching it now makes economic sense or just burns more gas.
4.title: Gas guesswork

problem.title: LPing should feel like yield. Too often it feels like ops.

trust.body: Stage 1 is intentionally designed to be low-friction and easy to trust. No execution, no magic promises, no fake automation story. Just a clean monitoring layer built to help serious LPs make better calls.
